definition: spaCy is an industrial-strength NLP library for tokenisation, part-of-speech tagging, entity recognition and dependency parsing.
details: Created by Matthew Honnibal in 2015 and developed with Ines Montani at Explosion.

explainer.lead: How to install spaCy, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

install.python: pip install spacy && python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm

quickstart.python:
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
doc = nlp("Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage in London.")
for ent in doc.ents:
    print(ent.text, ent.label_)

explainer.inAi: Fast entity extraction and sentence splitting for preprocessing; spacy-llm lets you plug an LLM in as a pipeline component.
explainer.jsNote: spaCy is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is a software toolkit that breaks text into words and labels grammar and names, built for real products rather than classrooms.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for production NLP pipelines and can plug in deep learning models trained in TensorFlow, PyTorch or MXNet through its Thinc backend. Prebuilt models cover 23 languages, so check language coverage before assuming a model exists.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source Python/Cython library under the MIT license, created by Matthew Honnibal in 2015 with Ines Montani at Explosion. It offers convolutional neural network models for tagging, parsing, text categorization and NER, with prebuilt models for 23 languages and tokenization for more than 65.

explainer.example: A team runs an English spaCy model to tag parts of speech and extract named entities from support tickets, then trains a custom tokenizer for another language.
